Entangled photon pairs at 1550 nm were distributed over 30 kilometers of deployed telecom fiber between two laboratories, with the source located midway. Polarization drift in the fiber was compensated by an active feedback system that monitored a reference signal multiplexed at a nearby wavelength; this kept the visibility of two-photon interference above 94 percent over a 72-hour run. The measured Bell parameter was S = 2.61 ± 0.04, violating the classical bound of 2 by more than 15 standard deviations. Timing synchronization between the sites used a common white-rabbit link, with residual jitter of about 80 picoseconds. These results show that entanglement can be maintained across existing infrastructure without dedicated dark fiber, a prerequisite for scalable quantum networks.
